svg.title: The one-page market map of the data and AI-data stack (SV-1), as of 2026-11-01
svg.desc: Nine horizontal layers stacked from bottom to top: infrastructure and object storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, Everpure, NetApp, Dell, VAST Data, MinIO); file and table formats (Parquet, Arrow, Lance, Iceberg, Tabular acquired by Databricks, Delta Lake, Hudi); catalogs and governance (Unity Catalog, Polaris and Horizon, AWS Glue, Dataplex or Knowledge Catalog, Microsoft Purview, Collibra, Atlan, Alation, BigID, Cyera, 1touch acquired by Everpure, Varonis pending sale to Proofpoint); operational databases (Oracle, MongoDB, PostgreSQL with Neon acquired by Databricks, Crunchy Data acquired by Snowflake and Supabase, Redis, CockroachDB, DynamoDB, Spanner, Aurora); analytical platforms and engines (Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Microsoft Fabric, ClickHouse, DuckDB with DuckLabs agreed to be acquired by AWS, Trino and Starburst, Dremio acquired by SAP, Teradata); pipelines and streaming (Fivetran plus dbt Labs, Airbyte, Informatica acquired by Salesforce, Confluent acquired by IBM, Redpanda, Flink, Airflow and Astronomer, Dagster agreed to be acquired by Prefect); semantic layer and BI (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Sigma, ThoughtSpot, Cube, AtScale); AI data (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus and Zilliz, Unstructured, LlamaIndex, Scale AI, Snorkel AI, MLflow, Weights and Biases acquired by CoreWeave); and agents and applications (Model Context Protocol, Salesforce Agentforce and Data 360, ServiceNow, SAP Business Data Cloud, Palantir AIP, Workday Data Cloud). Chip borders mark public companies (solid), private companies (dashed) and open-source projects or standards (grey fill). Arrows inside labels name the acquirer for 2024 to 2026 deals. Everpure is outlined in vermillion. A right-hand arrow shows value migrating upward from storage and compute toward catalogs, semantics and agents. Original diagram based on public information.
svg.text: The data and AI-data stack on one page (as of 2026-11-01)
Representative companies and projects per layer, bottom (closest to the bytes) to top (closest to the user). Not a ranking. "A → B" = A acquired by, or agreed to sell to, B (2024–26).

g.text: Value migrating up: bytes → formats → meaning → action
